q-162922.name: Question 1
q-162922.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=(6-xy)\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.
q-162922.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

Using the formula for ${I}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})(6-xy)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}6{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}y+6{y}^{2}-x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[2{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}y+6x{y}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}16-4y+12{y}^{2}-2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[16y-2{y}^{2}+4{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{4}]_{0}^{3} \\  & =48-18+108-\frac{81}{2}-0 \\  & =97.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is $97.5\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.$

q-162922.html:
Question 1
?

A rectangular plate occupies the region D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤3} with mass density function λ(x,y)=(6−xy)kg/m2, where x and y area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.

a
97.5kg⋅m2
b
87.5kg⋅m2
c
30kg⋅m2
d
95kg⋅m2
e
102.5kg⋅m2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

Using the formula for I0, we get

I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=∫03∫02(x2+y2)(6−xy)dxdy=∫03[∫026x2−x3y+6y2−xy3dx]dy=∫03[2x3−14x4y+6xy2−12x2y3]x=0x=2dy=∫0316−4y+12y2−2y3dy=[16y−2y2+4y3−12y4]03=48−18+108−812−0=97.5.

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is 97.5kg⋅m2.

q-163146.name: Question 2
q-163146.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=(x+y)\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the $y$-axis.
q-163146.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

Using the formula for ${I}_{y},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}(x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}y]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}4+\frac{8y}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[4y+\frac{4{y}^{2}}{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =12+12 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis is $24\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.$

Question 2
?

A rectangular plate occupies the region D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤3} with mass density function λ(x,y)=(x+y)kg/m2, where x and y area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the y-axis.

a
 18kg⋅m2
b
 32kg⋅m2
c
 16kg⋅m2
d
24kg⋅m2
e
 12kg⋅m2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

Using the formula for Iy, we get

Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA=∫03∫02x2(x+y)dxdy=∫03[∫02x3+x2ydx]dy=∫03[x44+13x3y]x=0x=2dy=∫034+8y3dy=[4y+4y23]03=12+12=24.

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the y-axis is 24kg⋅m2.

q-163170.name: Question 3
q-163170.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 1\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=(4y+1)\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.
q-163170.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

Using the formula for ${I}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})(4y+1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+4{y}^{3}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+4x{y}^{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}36y+9+12{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[18{y}^{2}+9y+3{y}^{4}+{y}^{3}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =18+9+3+1 \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is $31\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.$

q-163170.html:
Question 3
?

A rectangular plate occupies the region D={(x,y):0≤x≤3,0≤y≤1} with mass density function λ(x,y)=(4y+1)kg/m2, where x and y area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.

a
35kg⋅m2
b
23.5kg⋅m2
c
30.1kg⋅m2
d
32.4kg⋅m2
e
31kg⋅m2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

Using the formula for I0, we get

I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=∫01∫03(x2+y2)(4y+1)dxdy=∫01[∫034x2y+x2+4y3+y2dx]dy=∫01[43x3y+13x3+4xy3+xy2]x=0x=3dy=∫1236y+9+12y3+3y2dy=[18y2+9y+3y4+y3]01=18+9+3+1=31.

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is 31kg⋅m2.

q-163194.name: Question 4
q-163194.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132962/assets/2197dd68c567a5232ddf850b7ff8972033eb8cd0d11980baf6dc8e0a198b00a9.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $x$-axis and the curves $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt{2-x}$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=12y,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
q-163194.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,y\le x\le 2-{y}^{2},\,\,0\le y\le 1\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132962/assets/7a4216a2b1dc3859776c6589459d687981b79b123fa3a5eea638d31529e5cd3a.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-{y}^{2}}{y}^{2}\cdot 12y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{y}^{2-{y}^{2}}12{y}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[12x{y}^{3}]_{x=y}^{x=2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}12(2-{y}^{2}){y}^{3}-12{y}^{4}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}24{y}^{3}-12{y}^{5}-12{y}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[6{y}^{4}-2{y}^{6}-\frac{12}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =6-2-\frac{12}{5} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-163194.html:
Question 4
?

A plate occupies the region D enclosed by the x-axis and the curves y=x and y=2−x in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of D is given by λ(x,y)=12y, find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the x-axis.

a
 125
b
 94
c
 169
d
 85
e
 114
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

First, notice that D is a type II region with representation

D={(x,y):y≤x≤2−y2,0≤y≤1},

as shown below.

Using the formula for Ix, we get

Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA=∫01∫y2−y2y2⋅12ydxdy=∫01[∫y2−y212y3dx]dy=∫01[12xy3]x=yx=2−y2dx=∫0112(2−y2)y3−12y4dx=∫0124y3−12y5−12y4dx=[6y4−2y6−125y5]01=6−2−125=85.

q-163225.name: Question 5
q-163225.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14132962/assets/d1ef5062d5bc045c1e1f7fa58c513315852f74aa15539c001662b0055583f01b.png)

Consider the plate that occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the polar circles $r=1$ and $r=2$ and the polar rays $\theta =0$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=10x.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the origin.
q-163225.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (r,\theta ),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, note that the region $D$ in polar coordinates can be expressed as

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.
$$

Also, the mass density function in polar coordinates is 

$$
\lambda (r,\theta )=10r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}10r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}10{r}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =({\int }_{1}^{2}10{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =2{r}^{5}\,{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =2(32-1)(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-0) \\  & =31\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the plate that occupies the region D enclosed by the polar circles r=1 and r=2 and the polar rays θ=0 and θ=π4 in the first quadrant, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is given by λ(x,y)=10x. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the origin.

a
52
b
212
c
312
d
1522
e
23
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(r,θ), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by Ix=∬Dλ(r,θ)⋅r3sin2⁡θdrdθ.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by Iy=∬Dλ(r,θ)⋅r3cos2⁡θdrdθ.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is given by I0=∬Dλ(r,θ)⋅r3drdθ=Ix+Iy.

First, note that the region D in polar coordinates can be expressed as D={(r,θ):1≤r≤2,0≤θ≤π4}.

Also, the mass density function in polar coordinates is λ(r,θ)=10rcos⁡θ.

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the origin is I0=∬Dλ(r,θ)⋅r3drdθ=∫0π/4∫1210rcos⁡θ⋅r3drdθ=∫0π/4∫1210r4cos⁡θdrdθ=(∫1210r4dr)(∫0π/4cos⁡θdθ)=2r5|12⋅sin⁡θ|0π/4=2(32−1)(22−0)=312.
